title: hwp-styles-v1
description: The listing `hwp styles <file> --format json` and the MCP tool `hwp_styles` emit: every named style of the document with its resolved attributes and the paragraphs that use it. `attrs` has exactly the shape of the `style` level of `segment-envelope-v2`, and `used_by` holds `para` segment ids as `hwp cat --with-segments --segments v2` publishes them, so the two artifacts join on id alone. The listing is closed: a field added, removed or renamed is a new major schema.

contract.description: Names the contract so a consumer can tell this listing from the segment envelope.

styles.description: One entry per row of the document's style table, in table order, so an entry's array index equals its `id`.

id.description: Index into the style table, which is what a paragraph's style id holds.

english_name.description: May be empty: a document is free to leave it unset.

kind.description: `null` means THE DOCUMENT DOES NOT ANSWER, never 'paragraph'. The kind is the low three bits of the style record: HWP5 stores it there, and the HWPX reader maps `hh:style@type` `PARA` and `CHAR` onto the same bits. A reserved value is `null`.

next_style.description: The style id the document applies to the paragraph after one of this style. Published as stated, not validated against the table.

attrs.description: The style's own character and paragraph shapes and what they resolve to, the same object as the `style` level of a segment in `segment-envelope-v2`. A `null` block means the shape id does not resolve in this document's header table.

used_by.description: Ids of the `para` segments whose paragraph names this style, in segment order (the `segment-envelope-v2` order). Computed under default text options: a paragraph in a header, a footer or a hidden comment has no segment there and is not listed. The ids are not tamper evidence and not stable across edits above the paragraph, exactly as in `segment-envelope-v2`. A paragraph naming a style id outside the table is listed under no style.

style_level.description: One of the two style levels: the shape ids it names and what they resolve to. A `null` here is an explicitly absent block and never a fabricated default a consumer could read as the document's own value.

char_shape_id.description: `null` when the level itself is unreachable (an unresolvable style id).

para_shape_id.description: `null` when the level itself is unreachable (an unresolvable style id).

char.description: `null` when the character-shape id does not resolve in this document's header table.

para.description: `null` when the paragraph-shape id does not resolve in this document's header table.

char_attrs.description: The character attributes, in units a consumer cannot misread.

face_ids.description: Font id per language slot, in slot order hangul, latin, hanja, japanese, other, symbol, user. Seven are published rather than one, because picking one would silently pick a language for the consumer.

faces.description: The face name each slot's id resolves to in the document's font table, in the same slot order. A `null` slot means THIS DOCUMENT'S FONT TABLE DOES NOT ANSWER FOR THAT SLOT - the id is out of range. It does not mean 'no font', and a consumer must not read it as a default face.

size_pt.description: Size in POINTS. The stored value is HWPUNIT, where 1000 = 10pt; the division happens here once.

bold.description: From the character shape's own bold predicate, not from a re-derived bit test.

italic.description: From the character shape's own italic predicate.

color.description: `#RRGGBB`. The stored value is a COLORREF (`0x00BBGGRR`) whose byte order is a trap for a web consumer, so it is decoded here exactly once.

alignment.description: The decoded alignment as a name, never a bare integer. `unknown` means the document named a RESERVED VALUE: the stored field is three bits wide and the specification defines only 0..=5, so a hwp5 file can carry 6 or 7 and nothing clamps it on the way in. It is reported rather than coerced to a default, because a file we did not write is untrusted input and guessing `justify` for it would put a value in the envelope the document never stated.

indent.description: HWPUNIT (1/7200 inch); negative means an outdent.

line_spacing_type.description: 0 percent, 1 fixed, 2 margin-only, 3 at-least. It selects the unit of `line_spacing`.

line_spacing.description: Its unit follows `line_spacing_type`: percent for type 0, HWPUNIT for type 1. The pair is published rather than a resolved number, because collapsing them loses the distinction.
